cues.en: Hello. I'm John Fitch, MIT science reporter. We're at MIT's Lincoln Laboratory in Lexington, Massachusetts,
cues.zh: 大家好，我是 MIT 科学记者 John Fitch。我们现在位于马萨诸塞州列克星敦的 MIT Lincoln Laboratory，

cues.en: a major research organization which has played an important role in developing this nation's defense system since World War II. And although Lincoln Laboratory is perhaps best known for its work in radar and advanced warning systems, it has also seen the beginning of the computer era and has made many important contributions to it. To learn about some of its recent work in improving the relationship between man and this important machine,
cues.zh: 这是一家大型研究机构，自二战以来在国家防务系统建设中发挥了重要作用。虽然 Lincoln Laboratory 最出名的是雷达和预警系统方面的研究，但它也见证了计算机时代的开端，并做出了许多重大贡献。为了了解他们在改善人机交互方面的最新成果，

cues.en: we talked with Professor Stephen Koons, an associate professor of mechanical engineering at MIT and co director of the computer aided design project.
cues.zh: 我们采访了 Stephen Koons 教授，他是 MIT 机械工程副教授，也是计算机辅助设计项目的联席主管。

cues.en: John, we're going to show you
cues.zh: John，我们接下来要向你展示

cues.en: a man actually talking to a computer
cues.zh: 人是如何真正与计算机进行“对话”的，

cues.en: in a way far different than it's ever been possible to do before.
cues.zh: 这种交互方式与以往完全不同。

cues.en: Surely not with his voice. No. He's going to be talking graphically.
cues.zh: 肯定不是用声音吧？没错，是用图形来“对话”。

cues.en: He's going to be drawing,
cues.zh: 他会通过绘图来表达，

cues.en: and the computer is going to understand his drawings.
cues.zh: 而计算机能够读懂他的绘图。

cues.en: And the man will be using
cues.zh: 使用者将会使用

cues.en: a language, a graphical language that we call sketch pad
cues.zh: 一种语言，一种我们称作 Sketchpad 的图形语言，

cues.en: that started
cues.zh: 它起源于

cues.en: with Ivan Sutherland some years ago when he was busy working on his doctoral degree.
cues.zh: 几年前 Ivan Sutherland 攻读博士学位期间的研究工作。

cues.en: And you will see
cues.zh: 你将会看到

cues.en: a designer
cues.zh: 一位设计师

cues.en: effectively
cues.zh: 如何高效地

cues.en: solving a problem step by step.
cues.zh: 一步步解决问题。

cues.en: And he will not at the outset know precisely what his problem is
cues.zh: 他一开始并不知道具体的问题究竟是什么，

cues.en: nor will he know exactly how to solve it.
cues.zh: 也不知道到底该如何去解决。

cues.en: But little by little, he will begin to investigate ideas.
cues.zh: 但循序渐进地，他会开始探索各种构想。

cues.en: And the computer and he will be in cooperation,
cues.zh: 他将与计算机密切配合，

cues.en: in the fullest cooperation in this work. Well, now how does this differ from the way the computer has been used in the past to solve problems? Well, the conventional way,
cues.zh: 在这项工作中达成最充分的协作。那么，这与过去用计算机解决问题的方式有什么不同？以往传统的方式，

cues.en: the the old way of solving problems with the computer,
cues.zh: 也就是过去用计算机解决问题的方法，

cues.en: has been to understand the problem very,
cues.zh: 必须事先对问题理解得非常、

cues.en: very well indeed,
cues.zh: 非常透彻，

cues.en: and moreover to know at the very outset just exactly what steps are necessary to solve the problem.
cues.zh: 而且在最开始就必须明确知道解决问题需要哪些具体步骤。

cues.en: And so the computer has been, in a sense,
cues.zh: 因此在某种意义上，计算机

cues.en: nothing but a very elaborate calculating machine. But now we're making the computer be more like a... Almost like a human assistant.
cues.zh: 只不过是一台极其精密的计算机器。但现在，我们让计算机变得更像……几乎就像是一个人类助手。

cues.en: And the computer will
cues.zh: 计算机看起来

cues.en: will seem to have some
cues.zh: 看起来会具备某种

cues.en: intelligence. It doesn't really, only the intelligence that we put in it. But it will seem to have intelligence.
cues.zh: 智能。其实并不是真的智能，只是我们注入其中的智能，但它看起来确实具备了智能。

cues.en: In the old days, to solve a problem,
cues.zh: 在过去，想要解决一个问题，

cues.en: it was necessary to be...
cues.zh: 必须得……

cues.en: To
cues.zh: 必须

cues.en: write out in detail on a typewriter or in punch card form all of the steps,
cues.zh: 用打字机或穿孔卡片，把所有步骤详细地记录下来，

cues.en: all of the ritual that it takes to solve a problem. Because a computer is so literal minded? Because it's very literal minded. If you, for example, in the old days made so much as one mistake
cues.zh: 走完解决问题所需的全部繁琐流程。是因为计算机太死板了吗？因为它完全不知变通。比如在过去，哪怕你只犯了一个错误，

cues.en: of a comma in the wrong place or a decimal point that was omitted,
cues.zh: 逗号放错了位置，或是漏掉了一个小数点，

cues.en: the entire program would hang up and wouldn't run. But nowadays,
cues.zh: 整个程序就会崩溃、无法运行。但现在，

cues.en: if you make a mistake, you can correct it, as you'll see
cues.zh: 如果犯了错，你随时可以纠正，正如你稍后看到的，

cues.en: immediately,
cues.zh: 可以即时修正，

cues.en: and the computer is much more tolerant and much more flexible.
cues.zh: 现在的计算机容错率要高得多，也灵活得多。

cues.en: We met next with Mr. Timothy Johnson of the design division of the Department of Mechanical Engineering and asked him to show us this computer and its sketch pad.
cues.zh: 我们接着拜访了机械工程系设计部门的 Timothy Johnson 先生，请他向我们展示这台计算机和它的绘图板。

cues.en: We're at the TX2 console at Lincoln Lab. This machine is a large computer. It was built by Lincoln Lab in 1956 as a research machine. How does this differ from a computer that would be used to run your bank account or something like that? Well, it's designed specifically for a study of manual intervention where the man can command a computer to take different courses of action while the program is running. Running. We have several unusual pieces of input output equipment here. We have a scope, a knob, these are unusual at the time,
cues.zh: 我们现在位于 Lincoln Lab 的 TX2 控制台前，这台机器是一台大型计算机，由 Lincoln Lab 于 1956 年建造，是一台研究用机器。它和用来运行银行账户之类业务的计算机有什么不同？这台机器专门用于研究人工干预：程序运行时，人可以命令计算机采取不同的行动。正在运行。这里有几件不寻常的输入输出设备：示波器、旋钮，这些在当时都很特别，

cues.en: push buttons, toggle switches.
cues.zh: 按钮、拨动开关。

cues.en: We have several other related devices.
cues.zh: 我们还有其他几种相关设备。

cues.en: This made the TX2 a prime candidate for the sketchpad developments back in 1961,
cues.zh: 这使 TX2 成为了 1961 年 Sketchpad 开发工作的理想候选机器，

cues.en: and it remained a program in this machine so it would
cues.zh: 而 Sketchpad 也作为一个程序留在这台机器中，使它能够

cues.en: become a coherent partner in graphics so the man can communicate with the machine. How do you actually go about communicating with a computer in a graphical sense? Well, we are using an oscilloscope here which is much like a TV set except it's being driven by the computer.
cues.zh: 成为图形处理方面的协作伙伴，让人可以与机器交流。实际上，如何用图形方式与计算机交流？这里我们使用的是一台示波器，它很像电视机，只不过由计算机驱动。

cues.en: In order to get the information into the computer we have to draw somehow on this display
cues.zh: 为了把信息输入计算机，我们必须在这个显示器上以某种方式绘图

cues.en: and we use the light pen.
cues.zh: 我们使用光笔。

cues.en: Well, in order to construct a meaningful engineering drawing, have to have several graphical manipulations.
cues.zh: 要构造一幅有意义的工程图，就必须进行多种图形操作。

cues.en: Ivan's Sutherland's programs can draw straight lines and circles. Well, that's about what you do in the drafting equipment anyway, isn't it? That's very good start. In
cues.zh: Ivan Sutherland 的程序可以绘制直线和圆。这基本上就是绘图设备所做的事情，对吧？这是一个非常好的开始。在

cues.en: order to do this, we can position this bright spot in the middle of the cross that you notice at a desired location. We press the button to command the computer to draw a line. It will draw a line from this position where I am now
cues.zh: 进行这项操作时，我们可以把你看到的十字中心亮点移动到所需位置。我们按下按钮，命令计算机绘制一条线。它会从我现在所在的位置绘制一条线

cues.en: to any subsequent position of my light pen.
cues.zh: 一直延伸到光笔随后所在的任意位置。

cues.en: This is much like a rubber band stuck in two pins. One is nailed on the screen
cues.zh: 这就像一根橡皮筋卡在两根针之间。一根钉在屏幕上

cues.en: here and the other is at my light pen. So I can position this anywhere I want.
cues.zh: 这里，另一根则在我的光笔上。所以我可以把它移动到任何想去的位置。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: I lost tracking there. I moved the pen too fast, and that told the computer to stop drawing the line. Well, if you notice that bright
cues.zh: 我刚才丢失了跟踪。我的笔移动得太快，于是计算机停止绘制这条线。你会注意到，当我靠近那一点亮

cues.en: dot will jump onto the line as I get close to it. Well, the dot in the center of the cross, when you get close to the line, jumps over onto it. Correct. Why does it do that? It's much like a gravity field
cues.zh: 它就会跳到线上。也就是说，当你靠近这条线时，十字中心的亮点会跳到线上。没错。它为什么会这样？这就像

cues.en: at the end point. It is even a higher gravity field. It will allow us to position the point exactly on the line, or in this case, exactly at the end point. This allows me to move my pen quite coarsely, Be sloppy while I'm drawing and get a precision drawing out at the same time. So now I'm going draw a second line.
cues.zh: 在线段端点处存在一个引力场，而且那里的引力场更强。它能让我们把这个点精确定位到线上，或者在这个例子中，精确定位到端点上。这样一来，我移动光笔时可以相当粗略，画得不太精确，但同时仍能得到一幅精确的图形。现在我要绘制第二条线。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: even a third one.
cues.zh: 甚至第三条。

cues.en: Now, in an ordinary
cues.zh: 在普通的

cues.en: pencil and paper drawing,
cues.zh: 纸笔绘图中，

cues.en: all we have is this particular picture. But the computer understands the geometry of the drawing here. What do I mean?
cues.zh: 我们得到的就只有这张图。但计算机能理解这里的几何结构。什么意思呢？

cues.en: I mean that if I point at this particular point and tell the computer to move that point by another push button command,
cues.zh: 意思是，如果我指向这个特定的点，并通过另一个按钮命令让计算机移动它，

cues.en: it will move not only that point but all three lines that are attached to it. And
cues.zh: 它不仅会移动这个点，还会带动连着它的全部三条线。而且

cues.en: the delay between it's doing what
cues.zh: 在它响应

cues.en: you want it to
cues.zh: 你的操作时的延迟，

cues.en: is because
cues.zh: 是因为

cues.en: it's
cues.zh: 它正在

cues.en: computing all these changes. That's correct. Now
cues.zh: 计算所有的这些变化。没错。现在

cues.en: if I made a mistake, I could delete my mistake by pointing at
cues.zh: 如果我画错了，我可以指向出错的地方，

cues.en: the line in question for instance and pressing the appropriate button. It's gone.
cues.zh: 比如相关的线，然后按下对应的按钮来删除。这就没了。

cues.en: Now, I mentioned before we could draw circles also. In
cues.zh: 刚才我提到过，我们也可以画圆。为了

cues.en: order to do this, I must first indicate the center of my circle. Let's choose it to be here
cues.zh: 做到这点，我必须先指定圆心。我们选在这里，

cues.en: and then I'll move out to an initial radius,
cues.zh: 然后向外移动确定初始半径，

cues.en: let's say this point right here and I press the second button to start drawing the circle.
cues.zh: 比如就在这里，接着按下第二个按钮开始画圆。

cues.en: Here's our circle
cues.zh: 圆就画好了，

cues.en: and let me reduce the drawing size so our circle shows on the computer
cues.zh: 我来缩小一下绘图尺寸，让圆能完整显示在计算机

cues.en: scope.
cues.zh: 屏幕上。

cues.en: You see as I move the pen, it is ignoring the radial position. I've just gone off the scope screen here. The radial position of the pen, I'm only looking at its angular position.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，移动画笔时它忽略了径向位置。我刚才移出屏幕了。它忽略了画笔的径向距离，只看角度位置。

cues.en: It shouldn't be very as sloppy as you like. Right.
cues.zh: 你可以画得多随意都行。对。

cues.en: In other words, the computer supplied the compass
cues.zh: 换句话说，计算机在这里提供了圆规的功能，

cues.en: here much like it supplied the straight edge for the straight line. If you go backwards, erase it. And I can wind it up the other way. Now,
cues.zh: 就像它之前为画直线提供直尺一样。往回画就会擦掉它。我也可以反向画完它。现在，

cues.en: if I tell the computer
cues.zh: 如果我告诉计算机

cues.en: to put that point right at this circle right in that point right there, the
cues.zh: 把那个点刚好落在这个圆的那个位置上，

cues.en: computer knows that those must be connected.
cues.zh: 计算机就知道它们必须连在一起。

cues.en: It turns out that they're not really connected. It's a very small knob there. Let me move this away and show you that they're really not connected.
cues.zh: 其实它们并没有真正连上。那里有个很小的间隙。我把它移开，让你们看看它们其实没连上。

cues.en: But I am told that by terminating the point of the pin at that position that it must be connected.
cues.zh: 但我刚才把光笔停在那个位置，就是在告诉它这必须相连。

cues.en: Now I can tell the computer to satisfy this constraint command
cues.zh: 现在我可以让计算机满足这个约束命令，

cues.en: by bringing in a program under command of this toggle and watch this go.
cues.zh: 通过拨动这个开关调入一个程序，看好了。

cues.en: You see now that indeed the circle is ending at that line. We have constrained a drawing to behave this way. Well, wonder if you could expand a little more on this idea of a constraint. Just what do you mean? Alright.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，圆确实停在那条线上了。我们约束了图形，使其呈现这种状态。能再详细讲讲“约束”这个概念吗？究竟是什么意思？好的。

cues.en: Let me go to a second piece of paper. What I've done here is I really saved the way that drawing I just drew. You can get it back again? I can get it back and I can select my drawing number by these toggles here. So I've selected a blank piece of paper we'll call it. We have several pieces of paper.
cues.zh: 我们换第二张“纸”。我刚才其实把刚画的图保存起来了。还能调出来吗？可以调出来，我可以通过这里的开关选择图纸编号。我选了一张空白“纸”，暂且这么叫吧。我们有好几张“纸”。

cues.en: And I can
cues.zh: 而且我能

cues.en: let's I
cues.zh: 我们……我

cues.en: think it looks What something like
cues.zh: 我想它看起来大概是……

cues.en: I've done is I regard that first picture as a master. Mhmm. And I call up copy of it and I can manipulate it locally. I can reduce it, magnify it, and I can rotate it.
cues.zh: 我做的是把第一幅图作为母版。嗯。然后调出它的副本，可以在局部操作它。我可以缩小、放大，还可以旋转它。

cues.en: And let me place it right there. And I can do this several times. This is of course very instrumental for repetitive drawings like circuit diagrams
cues.zh: 让我把它放在这里。我可以重复做几次。这对重复性绘图当然非常有用，比如电路图

cues.en: or bridge bays where we have several repetitive structures. Oh, if you were drawing a circuit diagram, you might have little resistors or transistors or something already drawn and stored away and you could call up as many of those as you wanted. Right.
cues.zh: 或者桥梁节段，那里有若干重复结构。哦，如果你在画电路图，你可能已经把小的电阻、晶体管之类画好并保存起来，然后想调用多少个就调用多少个。对吧。

cues.en: Now, imagine that when I was doing my design work, I made a mistake in my master.
cues.zh: 现在，想象一下，我在做设计工作时，在主图里犯了个错误。

cues.en: Well, in order to correct that mistake, it would go back and let's say I don't really want this circular segment to be in here, I erase it.
cues.zh: 那么，为了纠正这个错误，就要回到主图，比如说我并不真的想把这个圆段放在这里，我就把它擦掉。

cues.en: Now I have the problem of making these changes to all the occurrences of this copy in my working drawing.
cues.zh: 现在问题来了：我得把工作图中所有这份副本出现的地方都做同样修改。

cues.en: This is very tedious nowadays with pencil and paper we have to remember where all the changes are.
cues.zh: 用铅笔和纸的时候，这非常繁琐，我们还得记住所有改动在哪里。

cues.en: Now you notice, you remember the drawing, that we now have lost our circular arcs. So if a manufacturer, for instance, some electronic part changed the design somewhere
cues.zh: 现在你注意到，你还记得那张图，我们现在已经把这些圆弧弄丢了。所以，如果某个制造商，比如某个电子元件在某个地方改了设计

cues.en: one of these years, you could just automatically change all the drawings in which it appeared? Voiceover: Correct.
cues.zh: 也许某一年，你就能自动更改所有出现它的图纸？旁白：对。

cues.en: Well, now I've showed you
cues.zh: 好，现在我已经给你展示了

cues.en: many of the basic graphical manipulations we have available. Voiceover: Incidentally, would like to ask you how big this piece of paper that keep you referring to is and how many pieces of paper you have available to you? Well,
cues.zh: 我们可以使用的许多基本图形操作。旁白：顺便问一下，你一直提到的这张纸有多大，你能用多少张纸？好，

cues.en: this scope, which measures about seven inches on the side, we regard this as a window that we can move over our paper and
cues.zh: 这个屏幕，边长大约七英寸，我们把它看作一个可以在纸上移动的窗口，而且

cues.en: enlarge the size of this window.
cues.zh: 可以放大这个窗口的尺寸。

cues.en: We can
cues.zh: 我们可以

cues.en: imagine the computer has a fixed sheet of paper behind this window. Its scale is approximately two miles in a size. Two miles? Right. Let's look at that. I can reduce this drawing slightly
cues.zh: 想象计算机在这个窗口后面有一张固定的纸。它的尺寸大约是两英里见方。两英里？对。我们来看看。我可以稍微缩小这张图

cues.en: and let me call up a copy of that master drawing again.
cues.zh: 让我再调出那张主图的一份副本。

cues.en: Put it over the center there.
cues.zh: 把它放到那里的中心位置。

cues.en: Oops.
cues.zh: 哎呀。

cues.en: Now I've hit one stop already. That's as small as you can. You're looking at the whole piece of paper, so. Correct. Mhmm. And let me magnify it now. And now it's magnified so it's practically off the screen.
cues.zh: 现在我已经到了一个缩放极限。这已经是最小的了。你看到的是整张纸，所以。对。嗯。现在让我放大它。现在它被放大到几乎超出屏幕。

cues.en: Place another one in there.
cues.zh: 再放一个进去。

cues.en: Sort of like the
cues.zh: 有点像

cues.en: picture within a picture within a picture idea.
cues.zh: 画中画中画的想法。

cues.en: Right. It's real nightmare material.
cues.zh: 对。真是噩梦般的素材。

cues.en: As you get smaller, even though the spot
cues.zh: 当你越缩越小，即使那个点

cues.en: sort of disappears,
cues.zh: 似乎消失了，

cues.en: it's really still there, isn't it? Right. The computer has this all memorized in its memory.
cues.zh: 它其实还在那里，对吧？对。计算机把这一切都记在内存里。

cues.en: Most of the things, though, that we live with in this world are three-dimensional rather than two dimensional pictures like that. Is it possible to use the computer in that kind of problem? Yes. We've expanded Ivan Sutherland's program into three dimensions. I have to bring that off the magnetic tape.
cues.zh: 不过，我们在这个世界上接触的大多数东西都是三维的，而不是那样的二维图像。能不能把计算机用于这类问题？可以。我们已经把 Ivan Sutherland 的程序扩展到三维。我得把它从磁带上调出来。

cues.en: There we have that now.
cues.zh: 现在我们已经有了这个。

cues.en: Here we have a single three-dimensional object
cues.zh: 这里是一个单独的三维物体
